ANTH312 Anthropology of Religion
ANTH313 Anthropology of Food
ANTH321 North American Archaeology
ANTH331 Human Evolution

Any ANTH course not taken to fulfill the above requirements.

Requirements:
To complete a minor in environmental science, a student must complete the following:
- Introduction to Environmental Science (EV100) or Introduction to Environmental Studies (EV150)
- One of the following: Ecology (BY320), Terrestrial Ecology (BY322), Aquatic Ecology (BY424) or Ecosystem Ecology (EV325)
- One of the following: Environmental Chemistry (CM371) or Atmospheric Chemistry (CM372)
- One of the following: Environmental Geology (ES330) or Climate Change (ES380)
- One of the following: Environmental Policy (EV311) or Environmental Law (LW270)
- At least three credit hours of coursework chosen from the list of approved electives.

A minimum of 9 credit hours must be courses not required by the student's major. A minimum GPA of 2.0 must be maintained in the courses taken for the minor. This minor is not available to students majoring in environmental science and policy or environmental health science.

Requirements:
The minor in humanities consists of six 3-credit courses (18 credits total) in at least three different disciplines in the humanities. The six courses must include the following:

One introductory course (100- or 200-level)
One course on theory or methods
Four additional courses in the humanities, at least two of which must be at the 300- or 400-level.

At least two courses must form a concentration in a single discipline, historical period, or thematic area, chosen in consultation with the minor coordinator.

Humanities disciplines at Clarkson include communication, history, literature, philosophy and modern languages.

Requirements:
Students in the minor in sustainable solutions for small island communities must complete a minimum of 18 credit hours, including 12 credits of core courses and 6 credits of electives. The core courses will give you a fundamental introduction to both the complex challenges facing these communities and the interdisciplinary approaches to problem-solving. Through your electives, you will tailor your knowledge to a particular area of interest, like environmental health or policy. You may not use courses that are required for your major to satisfy the requirements for this minor.

Required Courses (12 credits):
EV102 - Introduction to Sustainability for Small Island Communities
EV202 - Culture and Environment of Small Island Communities
EV302 - Case Studies in Sustainable Development for Small Island Communities
EV402 - Senior Design in Sustainable Development for Small Island Communities

Technical Electives (6 credits), select two from the following:
ANTH365 - Global/Local Issues in Food
BY314 - Tropical Biology and Ecology
CE340 - Water & Wastewater Treatment
CE479 - Water Resources Engineering
EHS309 - Global and Public Health
ES330 - Introduction to Ecology
ES340 - Environmental Chemistry
ES432 - GIS
ES436 - Ecological Economics & Policy
EV311 - Sustainable Agriculture
POL360 - Environmental Policy & Politics
SS232 - Environment & Society
Program name: Minor in Sustainable Solutions for Small Island Communities
